chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Samura ibn Jundab had a tree in the garden of a man from the Ansar, and the house of the Ansari was at the gate of the garden, and he used to pass by it to his palm tree and did not seek permission. So the Ansari spoke to him that he should seek permission when he came, but Samura refused. When he refused, the Ansari went to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him and informed him of the news. So the Messenger of Allah sent a messenger to him and informed him of what the Ansari said and what he complained about, and said: 'If you intend to enter, seek permission.' But he refused. When he refused, he bargained with him until he reached the price that Allah willed, but he refused to sell it. He said: 'For you is a tree extended to you in Paradise,' but he refused to accept. So the Messenger of Allah said to the Ansari: 'Go and uproot it and throw it at him, for there is no harm and no causing harm.'

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِيُّ: The man from the Ansar (Helpers of Medina)
key_terms.حَائِطٌ: A garden or enclosed plot of land
key_terms.سَاوَمَهُ: He bargained with him / negotiated the price
key_terms.عَذْقٌ: A single tree or a small cluster of trees
key_terms.لَا ضَرَرَ وَ لَا ضِرَارَ: No harm and no causing harm (a fundamental legal maxim)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal principle of 'no harm' (la darara wa la dirar) in Islamic jurisprudence regarding property disputes?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) resolves a property dispute between Samura ibn Jundab and an Ansari man, illustrating the practical application of the principle 'la darara wa la dirar' (no harm and no causing harm). The resolution involves a unique legal mechanism where the Prophet instructs the aggrieved party to uproot the offending tree and throw it at the owner, thereby transferring ownership and eliminating the source of harm. This incident is frequently cited by Shia jurists to demonstrate that the removal of harm can take various forms beyond simple compensation, emphasizing the flexibility of Islamic jurisprudence in maintaining social harmony.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Samurat Bin Jundab had a tree in a garden of a man from the Helpers, and the house of the Helper was at the gate of the garden, and he (Samurat) used to pass by it to his palm tree, and he would not seek permission. So the Helper spoke to him that he should seek permission whenever he comes. But, Samurat refused. 
So when the Helper went over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, he complained to him<sup>saww</sup> and informed him<sup>saww</sup> of the news. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sent a messenger to him and informed him with the words of the Helper, and what he had complained with, and said: ‘If you intend the entry, so seek permission’. But he refused. So when he refused, he<sup>saww</sup> bargained with him until it reached from the price what Allah<sup>ajwj</sup> so Desired. But he (still) refused to sell it. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘For you would be a tree extended to you in the Paradise if you accept’. But he refused. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to the Helper: ‘Go and uproot it and throw it at him, for there should neither be harm nor a harm caused’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Samrah ibn Jundab had a fruit bearing palm tree in the garden of another man from al-Ansar whose house was at the door of the garden and he (Samrah) would pass by when going to his palm tree without permission. The man from al-Ansar spoke to him and asked him to ask for permission whenever he comes. Samrah refused to do so. When he refused the man from al-Ansar went to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, complained before him and informed him of the condition. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, sent someone to call Samrah, informed him of the complaints of the man from al-Ansar and asked him to ask permission whenever going to his palm tree but he refused. When he refused, he (the Messenger of Allah) bargained with him and offered him a huge price but he still refused. He (the Messenger of Allah) then said, “In exchange for this you can have a fruit bearing palm trees in paradise”, but he refused to accept. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, then asked the man from al-Ansar to go, uproot that palm tree and throw it to him; harming and leading to harm is not lawful.’”
